messages:
sara: quick follow-up on the low-precision attention path — RFC suggested a fused dequant+attn fast path vs generic dequant+matmul. need to pick dispatch and rollout plan. any strong opinions?

Tom: i'm leaning pre-bind at model load based on shape/hw. avoids probe jitter at first request. can still keep a fallback.

li: pre-bind works but sequence length is dynamic. we should bucket seq_len (<=128, <=512, >512) and bind per-bucket. probe once per bucket on first use.

nora: important: KV cache layout must be identical across fast vs fallback to avoid copies when we fallback mid-stream. that means ABI contract for kv pointers/strides.

sara: agree on the ABI contract. propose adding a small kernel header version + capability flags so we can extend later without breaking old deployments.

Tom: what about per-tensor vs per-channel scales? fused path ideally expects per-tensor scale for broadcast efficiency. per-channel will complicate the fusion.

li: for INT8 we can do per-channel on weights, per-tensor on activations. attention fused dequant needs activation scale. so require activation per-tensor and allow weight per-channel.

nora: INT4 is trickier — packing/unpacking cost is non-trivial. the fused kernel should read packed INT4 directly and decode on-the-fly into accumulator registers, no intermediate float buffer.

sara: good point. implementation note: fused kernel returns float32 outputs but keeps kv cache in a quantized-friendly layout (packed or aligned) to minimize mem bw. fallback path converts to float32 kv.

Tom: dispatch heuristic: model metadata (quant profiles) + runtime probe (throughput delta) + config override. algorithm: prefer fused when (hw_supports_fastpath && seq_bucket matches && activation_scale_present).

li: also add a safety gate: if any eval prompt shows quality regression > threshold, automatically flip to fallback for that model version. tie to eval harness.

nora: on testing — unit tests should compare fused vs float baseline within tolerance across typical seq lengths + batch sizes. add synthetic worst-case where scales vary across tokens.

sara: rollout plan: canary to dedicated pools first (non-prod), compare p50/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and delta on per-prompt logits using our regression suite. then small percent in hosted, monitor errors and model quality.

Tom: metrics to track: kv-copy bytes, kernel time, end-to-end decode latency, token cost delta, and correctness diff (KL or token-match).

li: final infra detail: kernel registry API — we should register capabilities like "reads_packed_int4", "inplace_kv", "requires_activation_scale". dispatcher checks flags.

nora: +1. also ensure runtime has a fast path for zero-copy fallback: if fallback needed, avoid double-copy by swapping pointers if layouts compatible.

infra-bot: canary job queued: nightly-canary-lowprec-attn on k8s-dedicated-1 at 03:00 UTC.

sara: action items — (1) tom/ li: draft kernel registry flags + dispatch pseudo-code, (2) nora: write KV ABI header proposal, (3) infra: schedule canary and expose metrics. will sync w/ RFC authors tomorrow. :thumbsup:

Tom: i'll put a PR with registry sketch and probe logic.

li: i'll draft the seq_len bucketing heuristics and test plan.

nora: i'll add a short doc for kv layout constraints and a header proto.

sara: thanks all — short sync tomorrow 10am PT.
